Generate SCRU128, SCRU64 and KSUID values

Source: R/generate-scru.R
id_scru128.Rd

id_scru128() generates SCRU128 IDs by the specification's generator: 48 bits of milliseconds, a 24-bit counter_hi renewed once a second, a 24-bit counter_lo renewed each millisecond and incremented within it, and 32 random bits. Values from one session strictly increase; a counter overflow moves the timestamp forward instead of waiting.

Usage

id_scru128(n = 1, random = NULL, time = NULL, rollback = c("error", "reset"))

id_scru64(
  n = 1,
  node,
  node_bits,
  random = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  rollback = c("error", "reset")
)

id_ksuid(n = 1, random = NULL, time = NULL)

Arguments

n

The number of UUIDs.

random

NULL to draw from the operating system, or exactly the bytes needed: 10 per value for SCRU128 (4 of entropy, then the seeds of counter_lo and counter_hi), 3 per value for SCRU64 (the counter's seed) and 16 per value for KSUID.

time

NULL for the current time, or a POSIXct (or a double of milliseconds since 1970) of length 1 or n.

rollback

What to do when the clock runs back further than the tolerance: "error" or "reset".

node, node_bits

The SCRU64 node id and its size in bits, 1 to 23; the counter gets the other 24 - node_bits bits.

Value

A zuid vector of n values.

Details

id_scru64() generates SCRU64 IDs for one node, as the reference generator does: 256 ms ticks, then node in node_bits bits, then a counter renewed at each tick and incremented within it. node and node_bits are required, since only the caller can know that no other generator uses the same node.

id_ksuid() generates KSUIDs: seconds since 2014-05-13T16:53:20Z and 128 random bits. KSUIDs are not monotonic within a second.

A clock that runs back by up to the option zuid.rollback_tolerance (seconds, 10 by default) keeps the last timestamp, as both SCRU specifications recommend. Further back, rollback = "error" raises zuid_clock_error, so that monotonicity is never silently lost, and rollback = "reset" restarts the generator at the new time.

Examples

id_scru128(2)
#> <zuid_scru128[2]>
#> [1] 03h3wpqycpsgv19fiwwaug299 03h3wpqycpsgv19fiwyrqoku3
id_scru64(2, node = 42, node_bits = 8)
#> <zuid_scru64[2]>
#> [1] 0w4wsdo9pb42 0w4wsdo9pb43
id_ksuid(2)
#> <zuid_ksuid[2]>
#> [1] 3L8lrAezPT2QdJu7fICsDCPm5wC 3L8lr8qAgVo9p1qPWJkfdOrdnXE
